rubric_scores.justification: PAN is classified RESTRICTED in the Asset Inventory ('PAN (primary account numbers) | RESTRICTED | Card-Data Vault (RDS) | Yes — KMS AES-256'). L2 places the Vault inside a 'Restricted Data Zone' with KMS, and L3 puts it in 'RESTRICTED Data Zone (CDE core).' TM-005 'Tokenization detokenization abuse → bulk PAN exposure' is rated CRITICAL with OWASP Risk Rating 20 and a concrete step-by-step path (reach Tok per TM-001 → invoke detokenize repeatedly with enumerated tokens → harvest PAN at scale). The #1 top risk is TM-001 (flat trust → unauthenticated path to tokenization and PAN), which the rubric explicitly allows as the qualifying #1 ('this finding OR the lateral-movement-to-vault finding ranked #1'). TM-013 separately captures the over-broad KMS-decrypt/IAM angle. The concrete 'compromised service → KMS decrypt → bulk PAN' chain is present though split across TM-005 (detokenization abuse) and TM-013 (KMS key-policy too broad); the crown-jewel CRITICAL ranking, RESTRICTED classification, trust-boundary placement, and #1 ranking are all satisfied.

TM-001 'Flat internal trust — Tokenization/Payments callable without per-hop authentication' is CRITICAL (score 20), STRIDE-LM tagged 'S, E, LM' (covers both Spoofing and Lateral Movement), with a pivot path from a compromised CDE workload to the Tokenization Service. TM-002 also carries LM. Remediation R-001 explicitly states 'Treat the network as untrusted (zero trust).' The attack scenario describes landing on any VPC workload and riding the flat trust zone. Confidence HIGH, citing the prompt's exact statement 'JWTs validated at API Gateway but not re-validated on internal hops.' Both LM and S covered, zero-trust invoked, pivot path to Tok/Vault present.

TM-002 'Plaintext east-west traffic' is CRITICAL with STRIDE-LM 'T, I, LM' (Tampering present), attack scenario describes passive capture AND request injection/modification ('optionally inject/modify requests (no peer auth)'), and explicitly cites 'direct PCI-DSS Req 4 violation.' Stored-PAN protection is tied to PCI Req 3 in the Compliance Mapping (Section X: 'Req 3 — Protect stored cardholder data | PARTIAL') and in Positive Observations ('satisfies the at-rest portion of PCI Req 3'). PCI-DSS scope is acknowledged throughout, including a dedicated Section X compliance mapping table covering Req 1/3/4/6/7/8/10. All three sub-requirements satisfied.

TM-014 surfaces the analytics replication as 'PAN-adjacent transaction data replicated to lower-scrutiny analytics store' (HIGH), explicitly noting 'potential PCI scope expansion,' unmasked-PAN replication risk, and S3 bucket misconfiguration ('a misconfigured S3 bucket exposes the data'). TM-007 surfaces the Fraud-Scoring outbound call as SSRF/exfiltration/foothold (HIGH, CWE-918, OWASP API7/A10 SSRF) and TM-011 covers unsafe third-party consumption + availability dependency (OWASP API10:2023, fail-open/fail-closed analysis). Both halves of the rubric (analytics scope-expansion AND third-party fraud API) are fully addressed.

TM-003 'Admin Console refund/merchant-config functions lack fine-grained authZ / step-up' is HIGH, STRIDE 'S, E, R' (Elevation present), OWASP 'A01:2021 Broken Access Control / API5:2023 Broken Function Level Authorization,' CWE-862. Remediation explicitly recommends 'step-up MFA for refunds and config changes,' 'maker-checker (dual approval),' 'server-side per-action authorization independent of the edge JWT' — i.e., not relying solely on gateway JWT. TM-006 adds the IDOR/object-level angle. Maps exactly to the rubric's API5/A01 + step-up + internal authZ requirement.

All four DFD layers present as Mermaid: L1 Architecture (flowchart), L2 'Trust & Identity' with subgraphs for Internet/Edge/CDE/DataZone and a bold-red CDE boundary plus Vault in 'Restricted Data Zone'; L3 'Data (Classification + Encryption State)' with explicit [ENC]/[PLAIN] markers on edges (e.g., 'HTTP: routed requests [CONFIDENTIAL] [PLAIN]', 'HTTP/gRPC: tokenize/detokenize [RESTRICTED] [PLAIN]') showing plaintext internal hops; L4 'Threat Overlay' with risk coloring (highRisk/medRisk classes) and attack-path subgraph 'AP-1: foothold to PAN' with thick-red linkStyle edges reaching the Vault. The L4 overlay marks both Tokenization Service and Card-Data Vault as highRisk (CRIT, ffcccc fill). All R6 sub-criteria met.

Uses STRIDE-LM with OWASP Risk Rating (Likelihood × Impact, 1-5 each) and explicit severity bands in Appendix A (CRITICAL 20-25, HIGH 12-19, MEDIUM 6-11, LOW 1-5). MITRE ATT&CK IDs match the reference set: T1078 Valid Accounts, T1021 Remote Services, T1530 Data from Cloud Storage, T1195 Supply Chain, etc. CWEs include CWE-311, CWE-862, CWE-918, CWE-306, CWE-639. Critically, the output does NOT fabricate IDs — where a technique/CWE is outside the reference set (T1040/T1557 network-sniffing/AiTM, CWE-319, CWE-778, CWE-1357) it explicitly flags 'no matching ID in reference set — manual verification recommended' rather than asserting them. This adherence to the no-fabrication rule strengthens the pass.

All report-template sections delivered: Executive Summary with posture rating ('CONCERNING') + finding counts by severity table + top-3 risks + quick wins; System Overview; Architecture (Section III) and Risk Overlay (Section IV) diagrams; Asset Inventory (V); Threat Actor Profiles (VI) including 'External Attacker — Organized Crime (Card Fraud)' and 'Malicious / Compromised Insider (Ops Staff or Developer)'; Findings in TM-NNN format ordered by severity; Remediation Roadmap (VIII) with Waves 1-4 and explicit Quick Wins; Assumptions & Limitations (XIII). Every finding carries a concrete 'Recommended Remediation' step. All R8 requirements satisfied.
